argv:
Rewrite the text following the principles of Simplified Technical English.

Use one topic per sentence. Keep procedural sentences to twenty words or
fewer and descriptive sentences to twenty-five words or fewer. Keep paragraphs
to six sentences or fewer.

Use the active voice. Address the reader directly with the imperative for
instructions. Use only the simple present, simple past, and simple future
tense.

Use one word for one meaning throughout, and one meaning for one word: never
vary a term for elegance. Prefer short, common words over long or technical
ones. Do not use noun clusters of more than three words. Write out what a
pronoun refers to whenever there is any doubt.

Do not use slang, idioms, or metaphors.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
Operators must ensure the guard is lowered to within the recommended clearance of the workpiece before the blade is engaged, although the tensioning wheel should be checked periodically throughout a shift regardless of guard position, since drift in tension can occur even when the machine has not been used continuously. The lower blade guide must be inspected for wear whenever the blade has been changed, unless the replacement blade is of the same width and pitch as the one it replaces, in which case a visual check may be sufficient provided the operator has completed the tensioning procedure described elsewhere in this manual. Loose clothing and jewelry should not be worn near the machine, and long hair must be tied back. Operators may leave the work area only after the blade has come to a complete stop, though the machine's residual heat can persist for several minutes and caution is advised.
</passage>

response.text:
Lower the guard before you engage the blade. Keep the guard within the recommended clearance of the workpiece.

Check the tensioning wheel periodically during each shift. Check the wheel even if you have not used the machine continuously. Tension can drift over time.

Inspect the lower blade guide for wear after you change the blade. If the new blade has the same width and pitch as the old blade, do a visual check instead. Complete the tensioning procedure before you do the visual check. See the tensioning procedure elsewhere in this manual.

Do not wear loose clothing or jewelry near the machine. Tie back long hair.

Wait until the blade stops completely before you leave the work area. The machine can stay hot for several minutes after use. Use caution near the machine during this time.
